reconcile.note: Keil and Delitzsch separate the two judgments: the deferred sentence falls on Ahab's house because he repented, while the earlier prophecy targets his own life.

discrepancy.emptyNote: Steve Wells presses the inconsistency directly, noting Yahweh both spares Ahab for humbling himself and condemns him to die for releasing Ben-Hadad.

sides.snippet: your life shall go for his life, and your people for his people.
sides.verseText: He said to him, Thus says Yahweh, Because you have let go out of your hand the man whom I had devoted to destruction, therefore your life shall go for his life, and your people for his people.

sides.snippet: I will not bring the evil in his days; but in his son's days will I bring the evil on his house.
sides.verseText: See you how Ahab humbles himself before me? because he humbles himself before me, I will not bring the evil in his days; but in his son's days will I bring the evil on his house.
